title: lol-1998-galactic
label: Van Halent

won.source: The fed's own 16 April 1999 broadcast, recapping its own SantaSlam '98 finale: "we saw a brand new Galactic Champion crowned, as Van Halent knocked the Dodo off his perch!"

note: Carried the title across the fed's five-month 1998-99 hiatus and retained it through the whole of the fed's 1999 return, defeating a challenger by pinfall on 25 April 1999 and another by disqualification on 6 June 1999.

title: lol-1998-galactic
label: The Dodo

won.note: No winning date survives in the record; already billed champion before the fed's own SantaSlam '98 finale.

lost.source: The fed's own 16 April 1999 broadcast, recapping its own SantaSlam '98 finale: "we saw a brand new Galactic Champion crowned, as Van Halent knocked the Dodo off his perch!"

note: The title change is known only from the fed's own later recap; no document from the finale itself survives in the record.

title: lol-1998-orange-grove-texas
label: "The Loose Screw" Dmitri Damian Maku Stalin

won.source: The fed's own 6 June 1999 broadcast, called live by the announce team as it happened: "and NEW Orange Grove Texas Champion."

note: Successfully defended the title against a further challenger on 20 June 1999, the last show of the surviving record.

won.note: Already billed champion when the fed's 1999 return opens on 16 April 1999; no earlier winning moment survives in the record.

lost.source: The fed's own 6 June 1999 broadcast, called live by the announce team as it happened: "and NEW Orange Grove Texas Champion."

won.source: The fed's own 3 June 1999 broadcast, billing the pair the fed's first-ever undisputed Tag Teem Champions of the World after an elimination tournament for the previously vacant title.

lost.source: The fed's own 14 June 1999 broadcast, in which a rival pairing is crowned the new champions.

title: lol-1998-world-tag-teem
label: Bubbolicious Bob & Van Halent
note: The fed's own on-screen Chancellor held the title up on the 17 June 1999 broadcast rather than let it be defended by a team whose own partnership had broken up, and set a rematch for 28 June 1999 to crown new champions -- a date the surviving record does not reach before the promotion's second and final closure.
